[[File:James Monsebroten DecipherCon 1999.jpg|thumb|right|260px|James Monsebroten at DecipherCon 1999. Photo: Decipher.]]
'''James Monsebroten''' of Coquitlam, British Columbia, is a [[Star Trek CCG]] player. He placed 12th at the 2000 Star Trek CCG World Championship at [[DecipherCon 2000]], after reaching the 1999 World Championship at [[DecipherCon 1999]].<ref name="st00-deck">[http://www.decipher.com/startrek/deckdesigns/111700monsebroten.html Familiar Faces: James Monsebroten, 12th place – 2000 Star Trek CCG World Championships], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010210230841/http://www.decipher.com:80/startrek/deckdesigns/111700monsebroten.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="st99-finalists">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/stworldchamp/finalists.html Meet the 1999 Star Trek CCG World Championship Finalists], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011005154442/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/stworldchamp/finalists.html Internet Archive]</ref> Decipher photographed him at DecipherCon 1999.<ref name="fri59">[https://web.archive.org/web/20000612030624/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/photos/FRI/fri59.html DecipherCon 1999 Friday photo fri59], Decipher (Wayback 12 June 2000). Caption: "James Monsebroten of Coquitlam, BC, Canada looks like a winner"</ref>

== Star Trek CCG ==

=== 1999 World Championship ===
Monsebroten qualified for the 1999 Star Trek CCG World Championship by winning the Bolarus IX Regional. He was one of 32 finalists, with a rating of 1647.<ref name="st99-finalists" /> In the eight-game preliminary round he beat [[Ben Lacey]] in his first game and finished 13th at 8 (40).<ref name="st02">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/ST02_1.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Scores: 1999 ST World Championships], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001031210057/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/ST02_1.html Internet Archive]</ref> The top 12 went on to the Round of 12.<ref name="st99-final12">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/stworldchamp/final12.html Meet the 1999 Star Trek CCG World Championship Final 12], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000122121259/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/stworldchamp/final12.html Internet Archive]</ref>

=== 2000 World Championship ===
He won the Bolarus IX Regional again in 2000. As a regional champion he went straight to Day Two of the 2000 World Championship, where 29 seeded champions joined 38 Day One qualifiers.<ref name="st00-finalists">[http://www.decipher.com/tournaments/deciphercon2000/stfinalists.html DecipherCon 2000: Star Trek CCG Qualifiers], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010216105711/http://www.decipher.com:80/tournaments/deciphercon2000/stfinalists.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="st00-players">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/players/startrek.html 2000 World Finalists – Star Trek CCG], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001116224500/http://www.decipher.com:80/deciphercon/2000/players/startrek.html Internet Archive]</ref> He finished Day Two ninth at 11 (97), with five wins, a tie and two losses. His wins included games against Eric Johnfauno and Brian Sykes, who later met in the final.<ref name="st00-day2">[http://decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/results/startrek.html Day 2 – Star Trek CCG Final Results], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010303054446/http://decipher.com:80/deciphercon/2000/events/results/startrek.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="st00-decks">[http://www.decipher.com/startrek/deckdesigns/ Star Trek CCG Deck Designs: World Championship 2000 Finalist Decks], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010715205319/http://www.decipher.com:80/startrek/deckdesigns/ Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="st00-semis">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/players/startrek/startrek12.html Star Trek Semifinalists], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010127005400/http://www.decipher.com:80/deciphercon/2000/players/startrek/startrek12.html Internet Archive]</ref> He lost all four games of the final round of 12 and placed 12th.<ref name="st00-day3">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/results/startrek3.html Day 3 – Star Trek CCG, Game 4], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001026033417/http://www.decipher.com:80/deciphercon/2000/events/results/startrek3.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="st00-deck" />

Decipher published his World Championship deck, "Familiar Faces", among the 2000 finalist decks.<ref name="st00-decks" /> It played the objective Operate Wormhole Relays and the Treaty: Federation/Romulan, and seeded six missions: Cargo Rendezvous, Explore Dyson Sphere, Investigate Disappearance, Reported Activity, Sensitive Search and Study Cometary Cloud. Its ships were the Future Enterprise and the Starship Enterprise. Its personnel included Admiral Riker, Ambassador Tomalak, Captain Kirk, Commander Data, Mr. Spock, Albert Einstein and Sir Isaac Newton, with four Kivas Fajo - Collector and a Q's Tent side deck.<ref name="st00-deck" />

=== Team events ===
Decipher's Star Trek CCG team-events roster listed him on Team Hyperlight of Vancouver, in the Bolarus IX region.<ref name="st-teams">[http://decipher.com/startrek/tournaments/teamevents/teams.html Star Trek CCG Tournament Team Events: Teams], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000418003641/http://decipher.com:80/startrek/tournaments/teamevents/teams.html Internet Archive]</ref>
